From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

Hi Alex/Logan —

Need to lock a realistic beta plan + GA gating criteria for Usage Insights (cost drivers by route) this week so we can confirm staffing and set expectations with design partners.

Proposed (draft) timeline:
- Week of Feb 9: Phase 1 (pipeline + aggregations + API MVP) feature-complete behind flag
- Week of Feb 23: Beta enablement for 3–5 design partners (hosted + dedicated mix)
- Week of Mar 23: Expand beta (if SLOs + export performance are green)
- Target GA: week of Apr 6

GA gating (high-level):
1) Telemetry
- route + model dims fully flowing end-to-end (incl. fallback attribution edge case)
- cardinality controls (limits + rollups) enabled + alarms in place
- data freshness within published range (we need to pick the number)

2) Console
- route list + route detail stable, no major UX regressions, empty state + “Unknown route” guidance

3) Export
- CSV + JSON export, bounded by time range / rows
- audit logging for export create + download
- RBAC: org/project enforced; no cross-project leakage

4) DevEx
- SDK route tagging in Python + TS (Go if feasible)
- docs page + quickstart snippet + best practices for naming/cardinality

Two questions:
- Alex: can DevEx commit Monica + docs bandwidth to hit the beta enablement date? If not, what’s the least painful cut (e.g., ship beta with header-only route tagging, docs later)?
- Logan: do you agree with Feb 23 beta start given ENG-8421/8422/8425 dependencies? Anything that’s a hard blocker?

Attachment: UsageInsights_BetaPlan_GA-Gates_v1 (Google Doc link)

Thanks,
Marissa

—

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>, Nadia Rahman <nadia.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

Feb 23 is doable for “beta-visible” if we’re crisp about what we consider acceptable for design partners.

What I’m confident we can have by then (behind flag):
- route + model dimension ingest and join (ENG-8421)
- hourly + daily rollups with basic correctness checks (ENG-8422)
- top routes API + route detail API (ENG-8423/8424)

What is risky by Feb 23:
- export job timeouts for large ranges (ENG-8425)
- “late-arriving token metering” reconciliation story (we’ll need messaging; actual correctness will improve week-over-week)
- cardinality guardrails: we can ship enforcement, but we’ll likely tune thresholds after seeing real partner traffic

My recommendation:
- Beta criteria should require exports “work” but with strict limits (ex: <= 7 days, <= 50k rows) and very clear UI copy
- GA criteria should include export performance SLO + dashboarding (ENG-8430)

Also: we should explicitly call out in beta comms that “invoice ≠ console totals” within X% due to timing + retention and provide a short FAQ (Support is going to get pinged).

Logan

Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 11:14 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

We can support Feb 23 beta, but only if we keep SDK scope tight.

Proposal for beta:
- Route tagging supported via a standardized header in all SDKs immediately (no new typed param required for beta)
- Typed `route` option in TS + Python for GA (Monica can land TS first; Python is a close second)

Docs:
- Elliot can publish a lightweight “How to tag routes + naming conventions” page for beta (screenshot later)
- For GA, we’ll add the export report schema + troubleshooting section

Bandwidth reality:
- Monica: ~0.5 this sprint (she’s also on the auth refresh work)
- Elliot: 2–3 days this sprint for beta docs, 2–3 days later for GA polish

If product is OK with “header first” for beta, we’re good.

Alex

Date: Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 12:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

I’m OK with “header first” for beta as long as:
- console UI calls out “route is missing” and links to docs
- we have hard guardrails on route naming (length/charset) and cardinality

Re: gating, I’d like to make GA criteria explicit in PM-613:
- data freshness: 95% of events reflected in aggregates within 15 min (hourly view); daily rollup within 2 hrs
- API performance: p95 < 500ms for top routes view under expected load (plus query cost caps)
- Export reliability: 99% success for <= 7d exports; clear error codes for bigger

If that’s too strict, we should adjust now rather than post-beta.

Paula

Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

+1 to making GA gates measurable.

SRE asks for GA:
- dashboards exist and on-call can tell if the system is “lying” vs “lagging” (pipeline lag, late arrivals, export queue depth)
- alert thresholds tuned before expanding beyond design partners
- runbook for backfill/recompute is ready (with rollback)

For beta, we can tolerate weaker alerting if we keep the enablement list small and internal dogfood is on.

Allison

Date: Wed, Feb 4, 2026 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

On SDK ergonomics:

If we do header-only for beta, we should at least document a stable name:
- `X-Redwood-Route: <string>`

For GA, I can land a typed field:
TS example:

client.responses.create({
  model: "...",
  input: "...",
  route: "chat:summary" // maps to header internally
})

Python would match:
client.responses.create(..., route="chat:summary")

Two caveats:
- We need a normalization rule in one place (SDK vs gateway). If both normalize differently, customers will end up with duplicate routes.
- We should enforce max length and allowed chars client-side too (with a warning, not hard fail), otherwise the gateway will start coalescing routes and folks will be confused.

If Telemetry has a canonical normalizer utility, I can reuse it (or we implement the same regex in both SDKs).

Monica

Date: Thu, Feb 5, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

Summarizing decisions so I can update PM-613 + the internal beta checklist:

Beta (Feb 23 target):
- Route tagging: header supported + docs published
- Console: route list + route detail (with “Unknown route” empty/help state)
- Exports: enabled with strict limits (<= 7 days, <= 50k rows) + audit log events (create + download)
- SRE: basic dashboards for lag + export failures; no paging alerts until we see baseline

GA (Apr 6 target):
- SDK typed `route` field in TS + Python (Go “best effort”)
- Docs: full export schema + troubleshooting + invoice reconciliation FAQ
- SLOs: data freshness + API p95 + export success rate thresholds (Paula’s proposed numbers unless adjusted)
- Backfill tooling/runbook complete; feature flag rollout plan approved

Open tradeoff to resolve:
- If export performance isn’t stable by Mar 23, we either (a) keep exports beta-only longer or (b) ship GA with tighter export limits and commit to relaxing later.

Marissa/Paula — can you confirm we’re aligned on that contingency so I can word it cleanly?

Talia

Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 4:45 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta plan — timeline, GA gates, DevEx staffing

Confirmed.

If export performance isn’t stable by Mar 23, we keep exports under tighter bounds at GA (and document it clearly), but we do not slip the whole feature unless Security blocks audit/RBAC.

Also agreeing to Monica’s point: we need one canonical normalization rule. Logan/Nadia — please make sure the ADR/implementation is the single source of truth, and DevEx will follow it.

Talia — please update PM-613 with:
- beta gates + GA gates as you summarized
- contingency wording on export limits
- owners per gate (Telemetry vs Console vs DevEx vs SRE)

Thanks all.

Marissa
Director, Product (Console & Rollouts)
